1→# Session thirteen brief — W18 console token pass + W17 selected-choice outline
   2→
   3→Two deliverables, both CSS-level. Touch nothing else.
   4→
   5→1. **W18:** the operator console (`ui/index.html` + `ui/styles.css`) wears the Ryde theme.
   6→2. **W17:** on the party form, the selected Yes/No button keeps the pink outline
   7→   (`ui/party/party.css`, one declaration).
   8→
   9→This is a **token pass**: colour, typography and shape only. No layout restructure, no
  10→copy changes, no new DOM elements or ids, no behaviour change. `ui/app.js` must stay
  11→**byte-identical** (a test pins its SHA).
  12→
  13→## The design rule that governs every choice
  14→
  15→**Ryde pink is chrome. Status colours carry meaning and keep it.** The console tells an
  16→operator whether a ruling was delivered (green), withheld or human-only (amber), in error
  17→(red), or routed to a human / waiting on the party (blue). Those four keep their exact
  18→token values and stay on the rules that use them. Pink replaces the console's *decorative*
  19→blue and navy: headings, section numbers, the loader panel, the rider's claim quote, the
  20→advocate cards, citation chips, the event log's sequence numbers and actor tags, the focus
  21→ring. A withheld ruling must never read as brand pink.
  22→
  23→The canvas is **neutral** (the operator ruling): a warm light grey, not the party page's pastel pink.
  24→
  25→## What to build
  26→
  27→### 1. `ui/index.html` — head change only
  28→
  29→Add, immediately BEFORE the existing `styles.css` link:
  30→
  31→```html
  32→  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  33→  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  34→  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@400;600;700&display=swap">
  35→```
  36→
  37→Change nothing else. The font fetch may fail (offline demo); the fallback stack carries it.
  38→
  39→### 2. `ui/styles.css` — tokens
  40→
  41→Replace the `:root` token values:
  42→
  43→| Variable | Old | New | Note |
  44→|---|---|---|---|
  45→| `--ink` | `#182334` | `#31373E` | brand ink |
  46→| `--muted` | `#657085` | `#5A6470` | derived, same as party page |
  47→| `--faint` | `#8b96a8` | `#646C77` | derived: old value was 2.74:1, fails AA |
  48→| `--line` | `#d7dee8` | `#E5E0DC` | derived warm grey, same as party page |
  49→| `--panel` | `#ffffff` | `#ffffff` | unchanged |
  50→| `--canvas` | `#f3f5f8` | `#F5F4F3` | derived **neutral** warm grey |
  51→| `--navy` | `#213b5a` | **remove** | every `var(--navy)` becomes `var(--ink)` |
  52→| `--accent` | — | `#E93864` | **new**, brand pink: borders, rules, fills |
  53→| `--accent-text` | — | `#C8284F` | **new**, derived pink for small TEXT (brand pink is 3.7:1 on the canvas and fails AA for text) |
  54→| `--accent-wash` | — | `#FFF0F3` | **new**, brand pink tint for chip/header backgrounds |
  55→| `--shadow` | navy-tinted rgba | ink-tinted rgba | your pick, keep it subtle |
  56→
  57→**Keep exactly:** `--blue #2a638c`, `--blue-wash #edf5fa`, `--amber #9b5c18`,
  58→`--amber-wash #fff6e8`, `--red #a33f3f`, `--red-wash #fff0ef`, `--green #2e6b51`,
  59→`--green-wash #edf7f0`.
  60→
  61→Rule of thumb: pink **text** uses `--accent-text`; pink **borders/rules** use `--accent`;
  62→pink **backgrounds** use `--accent-wash`.
  63→
  64→### 3. `ui/styles.css` — chrome moves from blue to pink
  65→
  66→Each of these rules uses the blue as decoration today. Move it to the accent family and
  67→remove every trace of the blue family from it (`var(--blue)`, `var(--blue-wash)`, and the
  68→blue's own tints `#b9d3e3`, `#dceef7`, `#c9deeb`):
  69→
  70→`.loader-panel`, `.header-note`, `.section-index`, `.grievance-marker`, `.claim-text`,
  71→`.claim-card`, `.claim-card-header`, `.citation`, `.citation:hover`, `.event-seq`,
  72→`.event-actor`, `.event-row summary::before`, `#load-status[data-state="loading"]`.
  73→
  74→The driver advocate's card keeps its amber variant (`.claim-driver` and
  75→`.claim-driver .claim-card-header`): rider = pink, driver = amber reads as two sides.
  76→
  77→The focus ring (`button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible, a:focus-visible,
  78→summary:focus-visible`) becomes `var(--accent)`.
  79→
  80→### 4. `ui/styles.css` — status rules stay put
  81→
  82→Do **not** move these to the accent: `.outcome-ruled`, `.outcome-ruled-badge`,
  83→`.outcome-withheld`, `.outcome-withheld-badge`, `.human-only-region`,
  84→`.party-facing-region`, `.outcome-human-review`, `.outcome-needs-info`,
  85→`.routing-explanation`, `.citation-unresolved`, and everything else keyed to
  86→`--green`/`--amber`/`--red`. `.routing-explanation` is informational routing and stays blue.
  87→
  88→### 5. `ui/styles.css` — typography and shape
  89→
  90→- The `:root` font stack becomes
  91→  `Poppins, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif`.
  92→  Monospace stacks (event log, payloads, ids) stay monospace: they are data, not brand.
  93→- `h1`, `h2`, `h3` are set in `var(--ink)`. You may retune weights for Poppins
  94→  (600/700 exist; 720 and 580 do not render as intended in Poppins).
  95→- `.story-section` (and `.loader-panel` if you like) gets `border-radius` 12–20px.
  96→- `.citation` chips become pills (`border-radius` ≥ 12px).
  97→- The dark payload viewer (`.event-payload` and its children) may stay dark; retint its
  98→  hard-coded navy toward the new ink if you want it to match. Your call.
  99→
 100→### 6. `ui/party/party.css` — W17
 101→
 102→Add `border-color: var(--accent);` to `.choice-button.selected`. Leave `:hover` as it is.
 103→
 104→## Prohibitions (a test or review enforces each)
 105→
 106→1. `ui/app.js` byte-identical (SHA-pinned). No JS changes anywhere.
 107→2. No new, renamed or removed ids in `ui/index.html`. Only the three `<link>` lines are added.
 108→3. No copy changes. Every visible string stays exactly as it is.
 109→4. No layout restructuring, no new CSS files, no build tooling, no frameworks.
 110→5. In `ui/party/`, only the one W17 declaration changes.
 111→6. The old chrome values `#213b5a #657085 #8b96a8 #d7dee8 #f3f5f8` must be gone from
 112→   `styles.css` entirely, including comments.
 113→
 114→## Acceptance
 115→
 116→```
 117→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
 118→```
 119→
 120→Expected: **434 tests OK** (416 existing + 18 in `tests/test_console_rebrand.py`).
 121→The new file is RED now (12 failing) on purpose. Make it green by shipping this brief.
 122→If a test cannot be satisfied, or the brief conflicts with anything in the repo: **stop
 123→and report** rather than guessing.
 124→
 125→## Provenance note (for the record, not a build instruction)
 126→
 127→Brand values (`#31373E`, `#E93864`, `#FFF0F3`) are Ryde's real brand system, the same
 128→values the party page already uses (W10). Derived values are our own picks for WCAG AA,
 129→flagged as derived. The reference lives in the private planning repo and is not copied here.

1→"""Session thirteen acceptance target: W18 console token pass + W17 selected-choice outline.
   2→
   3→RED until the CodeBuddy build lane ships docs/session-thirteen-brief.md.
   4→
   5→W18 (the operator ruling 2026-09-27): the operator console wears the Ryde theme as a TOKEN PASS
   6→(colour, type, shape only) on a NEUTRAL canvas. The status colours keep their meaning:
   7→green = delivered, amber = withheld / human-only, red = error, blue = informational
   8→routing (human review, needs info). Ryde pink is chrome only, so a withheld ruling never
   9→blurs into the brand colour.
  10→
  11→W17 (the operator ruling 2026-09-27): on the party form the selected Yes/No button keeps the pink
  12→outline; before this it only appeared on hover.
  13→
  14→Written to the project's standing rule: pin the RULE, not the string. Every assertion
  15→targets a named selector's declaration blocks with comments stripped, so a decoy rule
  16→or a comment cannot satisfy it.
  17→"""
  18→from __future__ import annotations
  19→
  20→import hashlib
  21→import re
  22→import unittest
  23→from pathlib import Path
  24→
  25→REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
  26→UI = REPO / "ui"
  27→
  28→APP_JS_SHA = "e3ce88f05842a5ce7873bbaa6d576f7e88c2258dd3e7228b38c70d44ee1cc68a"
  29→
  30→CONSOLE_IDS = {
  31→    "loader-title", "case-picker", "run-folder-picker", "load-status", "payload-status",
  32→    "case-workspace", "case-summary", "summary-title", "loaded-file", "metadata-list",
  33→    "grievance-section", "grievance-title", "grievance-content", "evidence-section",
  34→    "evidence-title", "evidence-content", "claims-section", "claims-title", "claims-content",
  35→    "policy-content", "resolution-section", "resolution-title", "resolution-content",
  36→    "events-section", "events-title", "events-content",
  37→}
  38→
  39→# New :root values. Brand values from the private design reference; derived values are
  40→# our own picks for WCAG AA contrast on the neutral canvas.
  41→ROOT_TOKENS = [
  42→    ("--ink", "#31373e"),          # brand ink (was #182334)
  43→    ("--muted", "#5a6470"),        # derived, same as party page
  44→    ("--faint", "#646c77"),        # derived, AA 4.84 on canvas (old #8b96a8 was 2.74)
  45→    ("--line", "#e5e0dc"),         # derived warm grey, same as party page
  46→    ("--panel", "#ffffff"),
  47→    ("--canvas", "#f5f4f3"),       # derived NEUTRAL warm grey, deliberately not pink
  48→    ("--accent", "#e93864"),       # brand pink: rules, borders, fills
  49→    ("--accent-text", "#c8284f"),  # derived pink for small TEXT, AA 4.94 on canvas
  50→    ("--accent-wash", "#fff0f3"),  # brand pink tint
  51→]
  52→# Status tokens keep their exact values: the colours carry meaning, not brand.
  53→STATUS_TOKENS = [
  54→    ("--blue", "#2a638c"), ("--blue-wash", "#edf5fa"),
  55→    ("--amber", "#9b5c18"), ("--amber-wash", "#fff6e8"),
  56→    ("--red", "#a33f3f"), ("--red-wash", "#fff0ef"),
  57→    ("--green", "#2e6b51"), ("--green-wash", "#edf7f0"),
  58→]
  59→# Old chrome values that must be gone from the whole stylesheet.
  60→OLD_CHROME = ["#213b5a", "#657085", "#8b96a8", "#d7dee8", "#f3f5f8"]
  61→
  62→# Console chrome: every one of these rules used the blue as decoration. Each must now
  63→# take the Ryde accent and drop the blue family entirely.
  64→CHROME_SELECTORS = [
  65→    ".loader-panel", ".header-note", ".section-index", ".grievance-marker", ".claim-text",
  66→    ".claim-card", ".claim-card-header", ".citation", ".citation:hover", ".event-seq", ".event-actor",
  67→    ".event-row summary::before", "#load-status[data-state=\"loading\"]",
  68→]
  69→# Blue's own hover/border tints, which would betray a half-done swap.
  70→BLUE_FAMILY = ["var(--blue)", "var(--blue-wash)", "#b9d3e3", "#dceef7", "#c9deeb"]
  71→
  72→# Status rules that must keep their meaning colour (and must NOT take the accent).
  73→STATUS_SELECTORS = [
  74→    (".outcome-ruled", "var(--green)"), (".outcome-ruled-badge", "var(--green)"),
  75→    (".outcome-withheld", "var(--amber)"), (".outcome-withheld-badge", "var(--amber)"),
  76→    (".human-only-region", "var(--amber)"), (".party-facing-region", "var(--amber)"),
  77→    (".outcome-human-review", "var(--blue)"), (".outcome-needs-info", "var(--blue)"),
  78→    (".routing-explanation", "var(--blue)"), (".citation-unresolved", "var(--red)"),
  79→]

  81→
  82→def _strip_comments(css: str) -> str:
  83→    return re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", css, flags=re.S)
  84→
  85→
  86→def _blocks(css: str, selector: str) -> list[str]:
  87→    """Every declaration block whose selector list contains `selector` as a whole
  88→    selector. Raises when none exists, so a renamed rule reads as missing."""
  89→    found = []
  90→    for m in re.finditer(r"([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}", css):
  91→        selectors = [" ".join(s.split()) for s in m.group(1).split(",")]
  92→        if selector in selectors:
  93→            found.append(m.group(2))
  94→    if not found:
  95→        raise AssertionError(f"no CSS rule found for selector {selector!r}")
  96→    return found
  97→
  98→
  99→def _root(css: str) -> dict[str, str]:
 100→    block = _blocks(css, ":root")[0]
 101→    return {k: v.strip() for k, v in re.findall(r"(--[\w-]+)\s*:\s*([^;]+);", block)}
 102→
 103→
 104→def _luminance(hex_value: str) -> float:
 105→    h = hex_value.lstrip("#")
 106→    channels = [int(h[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (0, 2, 4)]
 107→    lin = [c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 for c in channels]
 108→    return 0.2126 * lin[0] + 0.7152 * lin[1] + 0.0722 * lin[2]
 109→
 110→
 111→def _contrast(a: str, b: str) -> float:
 112→    la, lb = _luminance(a), _luminance(b)
 113→    return (max(la, lb) + 0.05) / (min(la, lb) + 0.05)
 114→
 115→
 116→class ConsoleTokensTest(unittest.TestCase):
 117→    @classmethod
 118→    def setUpClass(cls):
 119→        cls.css = _strip_comments((UI / "styles.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).lower()
 120→        cls.html = (UI / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 121→        cls.root = _root(cls.css)
 122→
 123→    def test_root_carries_the_ryde_tokens(self):
 124→        for var, value in ROOT_TOKENS:
 125→            self.assertEqual(value, self.root.get(var), f":root must set {var}: {value}")
 126→
 127→    def test_status_tokens_keep_their_values(self):
 128→        for var, value in STATUS_TOKENS:
 129→            self.assertEqual(value, self.root.get(var), f"status token {var} must stay {value}")
 130→
 131→    def test_canvas_is_neutral_not_pink(self):
 132→        canvas = self.root.get("--canvas", "")
 133→        self.assertNotEqual("#f7dde3", canvas, "the console canvas is neutral by the operator's ruling")
 134→        body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, "body"))
 135→        self.assertIn("var(--canvas)", body, "body must paint the neutral canvas")
 136→
 137→    def test_navy_token_retired(self):
 138→        self.assertNotIn("--navy", self.css, "--navy is replaced by --ink everywhere")
 139→
 140→    def test_old_chrome_values_gone(self):
 141→        for value in OLD_CHROME:
 142→            self.assertNotIn(value, self.css, f"stale console chrome value {value} still present")
 143→
 144→    def test_text_tokens_meet_aa(self):
 145→        """Every text colour must reach 4.5:1 on each surface it sits on."""
 146→        surfaces = [self.root["--canvas"], self.root["--panel"]]
 147→        for var in ["--ink", "--muted", "--faint", "--accent-text"]:
 148→            for surface in surfaces:
 149→                ratio = _contrast(self.root[var], surface)
 150→                self.assertGreaterEqual(ratio, 4.5, f"{var} on {surface} is {ratio:.2f}:1")
 151→        ratio = _contrast(self.root["--accent-text"], self.root["--accent-wash"])
 152→        self.assertGreaterEqual(ratio, 4.5, f"--accent-text on --accent-wash is {ratio:.2f}:1")

 158→        self.assertTrue(stacks, ":root must declare the base font-family")
 159→        self.assertTrue(stacks[0].strip().startswith("poppins"),
 160→                        f"Poppins must lead the base stack, got {stacks[0]!r}")
 161→        self.assertIn("sans-serif", stacks[0], "a generic fallback must remain")
 162→
 163→    def test_index_links_poppins_webfont(self):
 164→        html = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", self.html, flags=re.S)
 165→        links = re.findall(r"<link[^>]*>", html)
 166→        self.assertTrue(any("fonts.googleapis.com" in l and "family=poppins" in l.lower()
 167→                            for l in links),
 168→                        "a real Poppins stylesheet link must exist (comments do not count)")
 169→
 170→    # -- chrome takes the accent, status keeps its meaning ----------------------
 171→
 172→    def test_chrome_rules_take_the_accent(self):
 173→        for selector in CHROME_SELECTORS:
 174→            body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, selector))
 175→            self.assertIn("var(--accent", body, f"{selector} must use the Ryde accent")
 176→            for blue in BLUE_FAMILY:
 177→                self.assertNotIn(blue, body, f"{selector} still carries {blue}")
 178→
 179→    def test_status_rules_keep_their_colour(self):
 180→        for selector, colour in STATUS_SELECTORS:
 181→            body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, selector))
 182→            self.assertIn(colour, body, f"{selector} must keep {colour}")
 183→            self.assertNotIn("var(--accent", body,
 184→                             f"{selector} is a status colour and must not take the brand accent")
 185→
 186→    def test_focus_ring_is_the_accent(self):
 187→        body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, "button:focus-visible"))
 188→        self.assertIn("var(--accent)", body, "the focus ring must use the Ryde accent")
 189→        self.assertNotIn("42, 99, 140", body, "the old blue focus ring must be gone")
 190→
 191→    def test_headings_use_ink(self):
 192→        for selector in ["h1", "h2", "h3"]:
 193→            body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, selector))
 194→            self.assertIn("var(--ink)", body, f"{selector} must be set in --ink")
 195→
 196→    # -- shape --------------------------------------------------------------------
 197→
 198→    def test_section_cards_are_rounded(self):
 199→        body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, ".story-section"))
 200→        m = re.search(r"border-radius:\s*([\d.]+)px", body)
 201→        self.assertIsNotNone(m, ".story-section must declare border-radius")
 202→        self.assertTrue(12.0 <= float(m.group(1)) <= 20.0,
 203→                        f".story-section radius must be 12-20px, got {m.group(1)}px")
 204→
 205→    def test_citations_are_pills(self):
 206→        body = " ".join(_blocks(self.css, ".citation"))
 207→        m = re.search(r"border-radius:\s*([\d.]+)px", body)
 208→        self.assertIsNotNone(m, ".citation must declare border-radius")
 209→        self.assertGreaterEqual(float(m.group(1)), 12.0, f".citation must be a pill, got {m.group(1)}px")

 213→    def test_app_js_unchanged(self):
 214→        digest = hashlib.sha256((UI / "app.js").read_bytes()).hexdigest()

  20→The Digital Native Track features real-world business challenges contributed by Ryde, a Singapore-headquartered ride-hailing and carpooling platform.

  34→#### Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution System
  35→
  36→##### Introduction
  37→
  38→Ride-hailing companies process thousands of dispute tickets daily — ranging from fare disputes and route deviations to property damage, safety incidents, and no-show charges.
  39→
  40→These disputes are complex, subjective, and emotionally charged, requiring human agents to manually review GPS telemetry, chat logs, photos, payment records, and company policy before reaching a decision.
  41→
  42→This current approach results in:
  43→
  44→- High operational costs — millions spent annually on human support hours
  45→- Slow resolution times — typically 24–72 hours per dispute
  46→- Inconsistent rulings — different agents reach different conclusions on similar cases
  47→- User churn — customers who feel unfairly treated leave the platform
  48→##### Problem Statement
  49→
  50→Build an autonomous, multi-agent dispute resolution system that can handle complex, multi- party conflicts between riders and drivers — gathering evidence, building cases, applying company policy, and issuing fair rulings quickly, transparently, and without human intervention for the majority of standard dispute categories.
